messages:
morgan: Quick sync — saw a sharp p99 spike under the 10k qps concurrency rehearsal. Correlated with a big burst of KV evictions and a rapid microbatch gate toggle. Putting raw notes here :frowning_face:

sam: Can you paste the grafana panels or numbers?

morgan: panels -> https://graf.redwood/infr/serving/d/xyz (short)
morgan: key numbers from the window: p50=40ms, p95=130ms, p99=480ms, cpu steal small, evict_rate ~7k/s, mb_size target=8 but gating oscillated 40<->120ms

jia: ran a quick flamegraph during the worst 30s, looks like we flip from fused-attention kernel to generic matmul around the same time. KV cache miss churn increases seq handling.

jia: snippet from profiler:
```
# simplified stack samples (top hot paths)
1) runtime::serve_loop -> kernel_selector::choose_fused (was hot)
2) kv::evict_hotset -> lock_contention -> memcopy
3) generic_attention_kernel -> slower path
```

leo: @morgan do we have microbatch logs showing gating decisions? Might be hitting the gating threshold because latency tail temporarily jumps and causes smaller batch windows.

morgan: pasted gating log (trimmed):
```
[12:34:56] mb_window_ms=6 samples=120 avg_lat=48 gate_open=true -> batch=8
[12:34:57] mb_window_ms=6 samples=900 avg_lat=140 gate_open=false -> batch=1
[12:34:58] evict_rate=7200/s kv_hotset=0.22 cache_hit=0.62
```

anika: So when cache_hit drops ~0.62 we hit longer per-request processing and gate closes -> tiny batches -> throughput collapse and kernel selector sees longer effective seq lengths leading to fallback kernel. That cascades p99.

sam: Could be hysteresis is too tight. Current MB gating: open if p95 < 80ms for 5s, close if p95 > 100ms for 1s. Maybe we need asymmetric windows or a minimum batch floor.

morgan: Agreed. Also kernel selector currently prefers fused kernel when estimated seq_len < 256 and cache_hit_rate>0.7. With cache_hit dropping to 0.62 fused gets disabled and generic chosen, which is ~2.8x slower on our hardware.

jia: Quick experiment results: forced fused on during the spike -> p99 reduced from 480ms -> ~220ms but p95 increased slightly. So fused helped tails. No memory OOM observed in the short run.

leo: Interesting. That implies kernel switch is a big multiplier. Maybe kernel selection should incorporate transient eviction flurries differently (e.g., smoothing cache_hit signal with EWMA over 10s).

infra-bot: [deploy] canary rollout completed for revision 3c2c.

anika: Proposed action items:
- Tune MB gating: add min_batch=2 and widen close window to 3s (to avoid oscillation).
- Smooth cache_hit signal used by kernel_selector with EWMA tau=10s.
- Add a short-circuit: when evict_rate > 2k/s prefer fused unless mem pressure > threshold.
- Add a perf regression check: synthetic burst test with kv-evict enabled in CI.

sam: I can take MB gating tweak today and run the 10k qps replay.

morgan: I'll push a kernel_selector branch with EWMA smoothing and the short-circuit. Jia/Leo can validate with profiler.

jia: Also created a micro repro script that simulates hotset churn + concurrent requests, will share in thread.

leo: We should log the chosen kernel variant in traces (span tag) so we can correlate kernel switches with tail spikes in SLO dashboards.

anika: Good note — add an alert runbook: when p99 > 300ms AND evict_rate > 1k/s tag as "eviction-wave" and run the kb checklist.

morgan: Thanks all. Will post results from the canary + replay later. :thumbsup:
